coverage.name: Lincoln County
limitations: Official sample ballots (all ballot styles, certified complete by the Clerk on Sept 18, 2026) read in full; sole county question is Ballot Issue 1A (Lodging Tax).

Lincoln County Ballot Issue 1A (Lodging Tax) raises the lodging tax and allocates the added revenue to purposes authorized under Colorado law; the question does not name housing, so no entry was created. Exact text: "SHALL THE CURRENT LINCOLN COUNTY LODGING TAX OF TWO PERCENT (2%) BE INCREASED $294,337 ANNUALLY IN THE FIRST FULL FISCAL YEAR AND BY WHATEVER ADDITIONAL AMOUNTS ARE RAISED ANNUALLY IN EACH SUBSEQUENT YEAR BY THE LEVYING OF AN ADDITIONAL FOUR PERCENT (4%), TO A TOTAL OF SIX PERCENT (6%), COMMENCING JULY 1, 2027, WITH REVENUE GENERATED BY THE ADDITIONAL FOUR PERCENT (4%) TO BE ALLOCATED BY A LOCAL APPOINTED BOARD FOR PURPOSES AUTHORIZED UNDER COLORADO LAW, INCLUDING CAPITAL INVESTMENTS IN PUBLIC OR COMMUNITY-BENEFIT PROJECTS, PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE, ESSENTIAL SERVICES INCLUDING LAW ENFORCEMENT, FIRE PROTECTION AND EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES, AND MATCH FUNDING OR OTHER ELIGIBLE INVESTMENTS FOR COMMUNITY PRIORITIES SUCH AS CHILDCARE AND OTHER PUBLIC PURPOSES AUTHORIZED BY LAW; WITH THE EXISTING TWO PERCENT (2%) LODGING TAX CONTINUING TO BE USED FOR ADVERTISING, MARKETING, COMMUNITY BEAUTIFICATION, AND EVENTS AS CURRENTLY AUTHORIZED; AND SHALL THE COUNTY BE AUTHORIZED TO COLLECT, KEEP AND SPEND ALL REVENUES RECEIVED IN 2027 AND EACH YEAR THEREAFTER WITHOUT REGARD TO ANY SPENDING, REVENUE, OR OTHER LIMITATION IN ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION OR ANY OTHER STATUTORY LAWS OF THE STATE OF COLORADO?"
Only other local question is Hugo Fire Protection District Ballot Issue 6A (fire mill levy) - not housing.
Sample ballot PDF is image-only; its text was read from the page images, with the county column checked by text recognition.
TABOR notice not posted as of 2026-09-26 (mailing deadline Oct 2).

coverage.name: Arriba (town)
limitations: Rechecked 2026-10-12: the Lincoln County elections page carries the same 'Certification of 2026 General Election Ballot Content' (dated 2026-09-18) and the same English sample ballots PDF (12 pages, image-only, PDF modification date 2026-09-18). The certification names no participating entities, and no TABOR notice or IGA list is posted. As read visually on 2026-10-10, the only local measures are Lincoln County Ballot Issue 1A (lodging tax) and Hugo Fire Protection District Ballot Issue 6A; no style has a town contest or question.

Town board minutes read 2026-10-12 (text PDFs): January 13, 2026: "Trustee McCue moved to approve the resolution placing the sales tax question on the Town's 2026 Ballot", a question "asking Arriba voters for approval to keep sales tax collected in 2025 that is in excess of what was estimated"; March 10, 2026: "Clerk Hart said she would be mailing out ballots on Monday, March 16"; April 14, 2026: "2026 Election Results" for Mayor, trustees and "BALLOT QUESTION 1". The town's 2026 regular election and its ballot question were therefore decided in April, not on November 3.

The May 12 and July 14, 2026 minutes and the town home page (checked 2026-10-12) mention no November 2026 ballot question; the home page's only election-related item is a trustee vacancy to be filled by board appointment on October 13, 2026. Minutes for June, August and September 2026 are not posted.

Closed under #2072: the town is absent from every Lincoln County style, and its own minutes show its 2026 election (with its only 2026 question, a sales-tax revenue retention question, not housing) was held in April.

Town of Limon trustee agendas for 2026 read 2026-10-12 (text PDFs except June 18 and October 1, which are image-only and were read visually): the February 5, 2026 amended agenda lists "Resolution No. 26-02-03; Authorizing the Town Clerk to Cancel the Regular Municipal Election Scheduled for April 7, 2026." The May 7 agenda lists the oath of office for three trustees, and June 4 an appointment to fill a trustee seat.

None of the 2026 agendas posted (January 7, February 5, March 5, April 2, May 7, June 4, June 18 special, July 2, August 6, September 8, October 1) lists a ballot referral, election resolution or IGA for the November 3, 2026 election. The June 4 agenda lists "Resolution No 26-06-12; Establishing Review Policies for Affordable Housing Projects", a board resolution, not a ballot question. The resolution text itself was not read, and the minutes page could not be opened on 2026-10-12.

Closed under #2072 on the Flagler basis: the town is absent from every Lincoln County style, and its own records show the April 2026 regular election was cancelled and no November question was referred.
